title: PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers need a trustworthy way to ask questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file without receiving non-deterministic or hallucinated answers from graph RAG or free-form LLM QA.

The current repository can extract a pyDEXPI full graph, persist a canonical base fact layer, derive an initial generic graph utility layer, and run a narrow pump discharge-path verifier. What it does not yet prove is whether Souffle can serve as the deterministic QA and verification engine over those generated facts.

The user wants to preserve the key product principle: LLMs may help classify, route, and explain questions later, but compliance answers must come from deterministic query outputs. Before adding any LLM integration, the backend must demonstrate that generated Datalog facts can answer useful P&ID topology questions, expose missing facts and predicates clearly, and preserve query results as auditable artifacts.

## Solution

Build the first deterministic P&ID QA query layer around generated derived graph semantics.

The solution should enrich the derived Datalog fact surface with enough base object facts to make query output interpretable, starting with node and node_label facts. It should add a small query corpus that records supported, unsupported, and future candidate P&ID QA questions in an engine-portable way. It should add a CLI query harness that runs a supported known-object topology query against an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file using Souffle, prints readable terminal output, persists the combined Souffle program, persists a JSON result artifact, and keeps raw Souffle output files in an internal output directory.

The first supported query should compare reachable targets and downstream_reference targets for a known source object ID. The first near-term unsupported query should be a pump discharge path classification question. A harder manual-valve-before-check-valve question should be recorded as a future candidate so the system does not overfit only easy queries.

The query corpus should explicitly encode determinism requirements and LLM role constraints. LLM integration is out of scope for this PRD, but the corpus should make future LLM routing safe by documenting that LLMs may classify questions, route to deterministic queries, and explain deterministic results, but may not produce compliance answers without deterministic query output.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to ask deterministic questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file, so that I can trust the answer is repeatable and auditable.
2. As a process engineer, I want QA answers to come from deterministic query execution rather than free-form LLM generation, so that compliance answers do not vary between runs.
3. As a process engineer, I want to provide a known object ID and see what objects are reachable from it, so that I can inspect the topology around a specific P&ID object.
4. As a process engineer, I want to compare reachable targets with downstream_reference targets, so that I can understand whether the generic graph utility layer is too broad or too narrow.
5. As a process engineer, I want query output to show full object IDs and object labels, so that results are exact and still readable.
6. As a process engineer, I want empty query results to be treated as successful answers, so that no-result cases can teach us about isolated objects or missing semantics.
7. As a process engineer, I want a warning when the provided source ID is absent from node facts, so that I can distinguish an empty answer from a likely wrong ID.
8. As a process engineer, I want the system to clearly say when a question is unsupported, so that I do not receive a misleading answer.
9. As a process engineer, I want unsupported questions to explain whether facts or predicates are missing, so that I know what capability must be built next.
10. As a process engineer, I want future thermodynamic or hydraulic questions to be identified as requiring external calculation when appropriate, so that Datalog is not overclaimed as a physics engine.
11. As a process engineer, I want the near-term north-star query to trace and classify a centrifugal pump discharge path, so that the QA layer grows toward realistic P&ID review tasks.
12. As a process engineer, I want harder valve-ordering questions to remain visible as future candidates, so that the roadmap reflects realistic engineering concerns.
13. As a maintainer, I want graph_facts.json to remain the canonical base fact layer, so that extraction output stays stable and auditable.
14. As a maintainer, I want Souffle to be evaluated as the deterministic QA and verification engine, so that rule answers can be fast and repeatable.
15. As a maintainer, I want Python to orchestrate extraction, Datalog generation, Souffle execution, and artifact persistence, so that Python is not the source of truth for compliance answers.
16. As a maintainer, I want derived_graph_semantics.dl to include node and node_label facts, so that Datalog queries can produce readable P&ID information without falling back to graph_facts.json for every label.
17. As a maintainer, I want the query harness to operate on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file first, so that the first slice directly tests the artifact users want to query.
18. As a maintainer, I want the long-term design to allow querying from graph_facts.json directly, so that later workflows can generate and query Datalog in one command.
19. As a maintainer, I want missing Souffle installation to produce a clear diagnostic, so that setup problems are not confused with query failures.
20. As a maintainer, I want Souffle syntax or runtime failures to be treated as failed query execution, so that invalid query programs are surfaced clearly.
21. As a maintainer, I want unsupported corpus entries to return structured unsupported diagnostics, so that unsupported questions are first-class product outputs rather than errors.
22. As a maintainer, I want the query corpus to be separate from compliance rule YAML, so that QA questions do not get confused with promoted validation rules.
23. As a maintainer, I want one YAML file per query corpus entry, so that each query can have its own lifecycle, documentation, and promotion status.
24. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include determinism metadata, so that the engine and source-of-truth assumptions are explicit.
25. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include allowed and disallowed LLM roles, so that future LLM integration does not bypass deterministic execution.
26. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include engine candidates such as Souffle and ErgoAI, so that the query library stays portable across deterministic engines.
27. As a maintainer, I want ErgoAI to remain a future engine candidate rather than an immediate dependency, so that the first slice tests the fact model before changing reasoning engines.
28. As a maintainer, I want the first query harness to read the query corpus entry minimally, so that the corpus becomes load-bearing without requiring a generic query interpreter too early.
29. As a maintainer, I want the first supported query implementation to be explicit and narrow, so that the team learns from real query output before inventing a broad abstraction.
30. As a maintainer, I want the combined Souffle program that actually ran to be persisted, so that users can inspect and rerun the exact query.
31. As a maintainer, I want the generated temporary query Datalog text included in the JSON result artifact, so that query behavior remains explainable.
32. As a maintainer, I want raw Souffle output files kept in an internal subdirectory, so that advanced users can inspect them while the top-level output remains readable.
33. As a maintainer, I want query output files to be overwritten during early experimentation, so that the learning loop stays low-friction.
34. As a maintainer, I want persisted JSON query artifacts, so that query behavior can become regression-tested and compared across fixtures.
35. As a maintainer, I want terminal output for the first query, so that hands-on learning stays tangible.
36. As a future LLM integrator, I want a query corpus with supported and unsupported entries, so that an LLM can later classify and route questions safely.
37. As a future LLM integrator, I want deterministic query outputs to be the only source of compliance answers, so that natural-language explanations remain grounded.
38. As a future rule author, I want the query corpus to reveal missing predicates, so that the P&ID query library grows from real questions instead of imagined ontology.
39. As a future rule author, I want the CodeQL-style library idea to grow from supported queries, so that raw graph facts become stable engineering predicates, reusable path predicates, and validation templates only when needed.
40. As a reviewer, I want the first query corpus to include a future candidate that is too hard today, so that the project does not optimize only for easy topology questions.
41. As a reviewer, I want the query corpus to classify unsupported questions by reason, so that missing data, missing predicates, external calculations, and ambiguity are not conflated.
42. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_missing_facts and unsupported_missing_predicates, so that the roadmap can separate extraction work from query-library work.
43. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_external_calculation and deterministic graph QA, so that thermodynamics and hydraulics are not accidentally oversold.
44. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between needs_human_clarification and deterministic query execution, so that ambiguous engineering questions are handled honestly.
45. As a reviewer, I want the first deterministic QA seam to be tested through the CLI and persisted artifacts, so that behavior is verified at the same level users experience it.

## Implementation Decisions

- The canonical base fact layer remains graph_facts.json.
- Souffle is the current deterministic engine for the first QA viability slice.
- Python remains the orchestration Adapter for generation, execution, diagnostics, terminal rendering, and artifact persistence.
- LLM integration is explicitly deferred until deterministic tools and query corpus semantics are established.
- The derived graph semantics output should be enriched with node and node_label facts.
- The first query harness operates on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file.
- The first supported query compares reachable and downstream_reference results for a known source object ID.
- The command should accept a query ID and load the corresponding query corpus entry.
- The command should support the first query ID with explicit implementation rather than a generic YAML-driven query interpreter.
- Unsupported query corpus entries should produce structured unsupported artifacts, not unknown-query errors.
- Missing Souffle should produce a clear diagnostic and failed status.
- Empty result sets should produce successful query artifacts.
- Source ID absence should produce a warning when node facts make validation possible, not a failed status.
- Terminal output should include full target IDs and labels.
- JSON output should include status, diagnostics, query metadata, source ID, generated query Datalog, combined program path, raw output directory, and result sets.
- The combined Souffle program should be persisted as a first-class artifact.
- Raw Souffle output files should be placed under an internal output subdirectory.
- Query output files may be overwritten during the viability phase.
- Query corpus entries should live under queries/corpus as separate YAML files.
- The first corpus entry should be compare_known_object_reachability with supported_deterministic status.
- The near-term target corpus entry should be classify_pump_discharge_path with unsupported_missing_predicates status.
- The advanced future candidate should be manual_valve_before_check_valve_with_exceptions with future_candidate status.
- Query corpus entries should include determinism metadata, current engine, future engine candidates, and LLM role constraints.
- ErgoAI should be documented as a future engine candidate for richer explanations, exceptions, and semantic-rule authoring, not adopted in the first slice.
- The long-term concept is a P&ID query library inspired by CodeQL: raw graph facts to stable engineering predicates to reusable path predicates to validation templates.
- The corpus should be engine-portable and should not make Souffle the only possible long-term reasoning engine.
- The near-term north-star query is pump discharge path classification rather than the more advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should verify behavior through public interfaces and persisted artifacts, not private helper structure.
- The highest test seam for the first slice is the CLI query command over a generated derived graph semantics file.
- Tests should run the query command against a representative fixture and assert terminal-visible behavior plus persisted JSON artifact shape.
- Tests should verify that derive-graph-semantics emits node and node_label facts as part of the generated Datalog artifact.
- Tests should verify that the first supported query returns successful output even when one or both result sets are empty.
- Tests should verify that absent source IDs produce warning diagnostics rather than failed execution.
- Tests should verify missing Souffle handling if feasible without depending on the developer machine PATH; if not feasible, isolate that behavior behind the command seam with controlled PATH configuration.
- Tests should verify unsupported corpus entries return structured unsupported diagnostics.
- Tests should verify the combined Souffle program is persisted and includes the generated query Datalog.
- Tests should verify raw Souffle output files are placed under an internal subdirectory.
- Tests should verify the checked-in query corpus entries include determinism and LLM-role metadata.
- Existing prior art includes CLI-style tests for export-facts, derive-graph-semantics, verify-suite, verify-raw-fixture, and compile-rule.
- Existing prior art also includes persisted artifact assertions for graph facts, derived graph semantics, verifier results, and behavioral harness summaries.
- The tests should extend those existing black-box seams rather than introducing internal mocks.
- The first implementation should use red-green vertical slices: one behavior test, minimal implementation, repeat.

## Out of Scope

- LLM integration.
- Natural-language question classification.
- RAG or MCP routing.
- OmniTQA implementation.
- ErgoAI integration.
- A generic query language interpreter over YAML corpus files.
- Full support for arbitrary user-generated P&ID questions.
- Full compliance rule authoring.
- Thermodynamic, hydraulic, sizing, or simulation calculations.
- DEXPI 2.0 ingestion.
- Replacing graph_facts.json as the canonical base fact layer.
- Making Python the source of truth for compliance answers.
- Immutable production run directories for query artifacts.
- A polished process engineer UI.
- Full path provenance or ordered path reconstruction beyond what the first query needs.
- Supporting the advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query in the first slice.
- Promoting unsupported corpus entries to trusted validation rules.

## Further Notes

The key product principle is: the LLM can help ask, route, and explain the question, but deterministic tools must answer compliance questions.

The first implementation should be treated as a Souffle QA viability slice. It should be allowed to reveal that current predicates are too broad, too narrow, or missing. That learning is valuable and should drive the next predicates in the P&ID query library.

The strongest external architecture analogues are CodeQL for layered query libraries and query metadata, OPA for deterministic policy decisions and diagnostics, osquery for exposing messy domain state through stable queryable relations, and Semgrep or dbt-style registries for curated query/rule corpora with examples and tests.

The most important immediate learning is whether generated Datalog artifacts can support useful known-object topology QA before the project invests in YAML-to-rule compilation, LLM routing, or a larger semantic-rule engine.

title: Emit human-readable node alias facts in derived graph semantics
description:
Add a thin alias layer to derived graph semantics so deterministic QA can keep node_id as the canonical topology key while exposing human-readable selectors for tests and terminal output.

Context:
- Parent PRD: pydexpi-datalog-1-153 Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer.
- Current derived semantics emits node/1 and node_label/2 from graph_facts.json.
- UUID node IDs are correct for graph joins but hard for humans to inspect against P&ID/SVG/XML views.

What to build:
- Keep node_id as the canonical graph identity.
- Emit node_tag(id, tag) facts from node attribute tagName when present.
- Emit node_proteus_id(id, proteus_id) facts from node attribute proteusId when present.
- Consider emitting node_display_name(id, display) with a narrow deterministic fallback order: tagName, then proteusId, then label.
- Do not replace node_id in existing predicates.
- Do not parse SVG labels or introduce a generic identity resolver in this slice.

Acceptance criteria:
- derive-graph-semantics emits node_tag/2 for tagged graph objects.
- derive-graph-semantics emits node_proteus_id/2 for objects with proteusId.
- If node_display_name/2 is included, its fallback order is documented and tested.
- Existing node/1, node_label/2, and edge-family predicates continue to be emitted unchanged.
- Tests verify behavior through the CLI-generated derived_graph_semantics.dl artifact using representative graph_facts.json.
- Representative generated artifact is updated if this repo keeps one checked in.
close_reason: Completed: derive-graph-semantics now emits node_tag/2 from tagName and node_proteus_id/2 from proteusId while keeping node_id as the canonical graph identity. Updated representative derived_graph_semantics.dl, CLI artifact tests, and the derived graph semantics contract. Validation passed: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_derive_graph_semantics.py (4 tests OK) and .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests (58 tests OK).

title: Define stable reported result schemas for graph-based rule evaluation
description:
## Parent

- PRD: GitHub issue #1 "Build graph-to-facts Datalog verifier on top of a pyDEXPI fork"

## What to build

Define the stable reported result schemas for graph-based rule evaluation over the first discharge-path rule family.

Given graph-mirrored facts and compiled Datalog rules, lock the machine-readable output shapes for `pass`, `hard_violation`, `bounded_failure_off_page`, and `evaluation_diagnostic`. Each result shape must carry deterministic evidence about the traversed path, matched objects, matched edges, boundary kind, and short human-readable explanation.

This slice should make the reporting model concrete before the fixture suite is expanded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stable machine-readable result schemas exist for `pass`, `hard_violation`, `bounded_failure_off_page`, and `evaluation_diagnostic`.
- [ ] Example output artifacts exist for each result shape and show the required path and boundary evidence.
- [ ] The required evidence for each result shape is documented, including matched objects, traversed edges, terminal boundary, and human-readable message.
- [ ] The result shapes are deterministic enough to be reused as golden outputs in later fixture-driven tests.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2xn
close_reason: Defined stable result schema validator, checked in pass/hard_violation/bounded_failure_off_page/evaluation_diagnostic examples, and documented required evidence; validated with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests

title: Derive and compare direct process connection semantics
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Add the first CodeQL-like predicate-library experiment for P&ID topology. This slice should derive an experimental direct_process_connection predicate from the current graph semantics, run comparison queries against representative fixtures, and persist evidence showing whether it improves over lower-level downstream_reference and reachable predicates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A direct_process_connection predicate is derived as an experimental process-facing relation.
- [ ] The query harness can compare direct_process_connection results against downstream_reference and reachable results for representative known source IDs.
- [ ] Comparison output is persisted as JSON and printed in a readable terminal form.
- [ ] The implementation does not claim the predicate is final or fully trusted process flow semantics.
- [ ] The result artifact makes it clear whether direct_process_connection appears broader, narrower, or more useful than lower-level predicates on the tested fixtures.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-su1
- pydexpi-datalog-1-93c

title: Establish the graph-to-facts contract from pinned pyDEXPI outputs
description:
## Parent

- PRD: GitHub issue #1 "Build graph-to-facts Datalog verifier on top of a pyDEXPI fork"

## What to build

Establish the project-owned graph-to-facts contract over pinned `pyDEXPI` output for several real DEXPI 1.3 pump-related examples already in the repo.

Treat `pyDEXPI` as a trusted extraction dependency whose behavior is observed and contract-tested, not re-proven. Define the graph-mirrored fact vocabulary, document the contract, and persist golden input/output pairs so future work can diff graph facts against known-good outputs.

This slice should make it obvious how real `pyDEXPI` graph output becomes project facts, and should produce concrete acceptance artifacts rather than an abstract design note.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pinned `pyDEXPI` fork reference or version is recorded for this repo's verifier work.
- [ ] A graph-to-facts contract document exists and explains the project-owned graph-mirrored fact vocabulary.
- [ ] Several real DEXPI 1.3 pump-related examples in the repo produce persisted golden fact outputs that can be diffed in future regressions.
- [ ] The slice demonstrates one-to-one preservation between selected graph structures and emitted base facts without hidden verifier-specific simplification.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.
close_reason: Implemented export-facts CLI over vendored pyDEXPI, checked in graph-to-facts contract docs and golden fixtures, and validated with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests

title: Return structured unsupported query corpus results
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Allow the query command to run against unsupported or future-candidate corpus entries and return structured unsupported results instead of treating them as unknown or failed queries. This slice should prove unsupported questions are first-class product outputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running an unsupported missing-predicates corpus entry returns a structured unsupported result artifact.
- [ ] Running a future-candidate corpus entry returns a structured future-candidate result artifact.
- [ ] Unsupported diagnostics include missing facts, missing predicates, external-calculation needs, or ambiguity reasons when recorded in the corpus.
- [ ] Unsupported query handling uses the same CLI and artifact seam as supported queries.
- [ ] Unsupported results do not invoke Souffle unless a supported implementation exists for that query.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-3j4
- pydexpi-datalog-1-93c

title: Define the minimal YAML rule format and compile it into Souffle-style Datalog
description:
## Parent

- PRD: GitHub issue #1 "Build graph-to-facts Datalog verifier on top of a pyDEXPI fork"

## What to build

Define the minimal semi-structured YAML rule format for the first discharge-path tracer bullet, rooted in actual pump discharge patterns visible in the repo's DEXPI 1.3 examples.

Do not design a general rule language yet. Keep the YAML intentionally small and focused on what the first discharge-path rules need. Then compile at least one real YAML rule into a concrete Souffle-style Datalog representation and make the translation visible so the team can inspect both input and output.

This slice exists to make the operator-facing rule format and the Datalog compilation output concrete and reviewable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A minimal YAML rule schema exists for the discharge-path rule family and is intentionally scoped to the first tracer bullet rather than a general-purpose language.
- [ ] At least one real discharge-path YAML rule file derived from actual repo examples validates successfully.
- [ ] At least one invalid YAML rule example fails with deterministic validation output.
- [ ] The valid YAML rule compiles into visible Souffle-style Datalog output that can be inspected side by side with the YAML input.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2xnne
close_reason: Implemented compile-rule CLI, minimal pump discharge YAML schema, deterministic invalid-rule validation, and checked-in Souffle-style Datalog artifacts; validated with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests

title: Add a Souffle-backed derived semantics query harness
description:
## What to build

Add the first deterministic P&ID QA query harness over generated derived graph semantics.

This slice should prove that Souffle can answer one useful known-object topology QA question over generated Datalog artifacts, while keeping the query corpus engine-portable for future deterministic engines such as ErgoAI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `derive-graph-semantics` emits `node/1` and `node_label/2` facts alongside existing graph predicates.
- [ ] A checked-in query corpus exists under `queries/corpus/` with separate YAML entries for:
  - `compare_known_object_reachability` as `supported_deterministic`
  - `classify_pump_discharge_path` as `unsupported_missing_predicates`
  - `manual_valve_before_check_valve_with_exceptions` as `future_candidate`
- [ ] Corpus entries include determinism and LLM-role metadata stating that LLMs may classify/route/explain but cannot answer compliance questions without deterministic query results.
- [ ] A CLI command can query an existing `derived_graph_semantics.dl` with a known `source_id`.
- [ ] The first supported query compares `reachable/2` and `downstream_reference/2` side by side.
- [ ] The command detects missing `souffle` and emits a clear diagnostic.
- [ ] Empty result sets are successful query results.
- [ ] If `node/1` is available and the source ID is absent, the command returns success with a warning diagnostic.
- [ ] The command prints full target IDs plus labels to the terminal.
- [ ] The command persists:
  - combined Souffle program
  - JSON result artifact
  - raw Souffle output files under an internal subdirectory
- [ ] Unsupported corpus entries return structured unsupported diagnostics, not unknown-query errors.

## Notes

This bead intentionally defers LLM integration. Python should orchestrate Datalog generation, Souffle execution, and artifact persistence; deterministic query output remains the source of truth.
close_reason: Superseded by smaller vertical slices under pydexpi-datalog-1-153.

title: Add multi-rule execution and overlapping finding reporting
description:
## Parent

- PRD: GitHub issue #1 "Build graph-to-facts Datalog verifier on top of a pyDEXPI fork"

## What to build

Add multi-rule execution and overlapping finding reporting for the first verifier slice.

Run at least two real or minimally adapted rules against the same fixture set and prove that the verifier can report multiple findings deterministically, including cases where rules touch overlapping graph regions. This slice is still detection-only: no hypothetical edits are applied and no post-edit re-evaluation is performed yet. The goal is to prove that multiple rules can coexist in one run and still produce stable, inspectable outputs.

This slice should make rule interaction visible without taking on patch application semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least two real or minimally adapted rules execute against the same fixture set in one run.
- [ ] At least one fixture produces findings from both rules on overlapping graph regions.
- [ ] Output artifacts show how multiple findings are reported together in one deterministic run.
- [ ] The documented result model makes it explicit that multi-rule detection is supported while hypothetical post-edit re-evaluation is deferred.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-7bq
close_reason: Added multi-rule verify-suite support, overlapping E06 finding artifact, and deferred reevaluation documentation; validated with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests

title: Sweep the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus through export-facts
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-n2o "PRD: Establish the DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate and derived Souffle semantics"

## What to build

Run the canonical base fact layer against the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus rather than only the current golden seed set.

This slice should prove that the repository can take real DEXPI 1.3 source fixtures end to end through `pyDEXPI` extraction and graph-mirrored fact export, while making corpus coverage visible and reproducible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus is enumerated and exercised through the export seam.
- [ ] The slice makes it obvious which fixtures parse successfully, which fail, and which are intentionally excluded.
- [ ] The resulting coverage is demoable through persisted artifacts or deterministic summaries rather than an informal claim.

title: PRD: Establish the DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate and derived Souffle semantics
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineering teams need a deterministic substrate for logical
programming over DEXPI 1.3 P&IDs before they can trust richer operator-facing
verification workflows.

The current repository already has useful scaffolding, a graph-mirrored export
seed, and an initial tracer-bullet verifier. What it does not yet have is a
fully explicit contract for turning the supported DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus into
graph-mirrored facts and then deriving reusable Souffle semantics from those
facts. Without that substrate, later rule work risks drifting into ad hoc
predicate design, fixture-specific shortcuts, or AI-generated rules without a
stable deterministic execution boundary.

## Solution

Build the next verifier substrate slice around DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored facts
and derived Souffle graph semantics.

The solution should treat `pyDEXPI` as the trusted extraction dependency for
DEXPI 1.3 XML-to-graph conversion, persist a verbose and generic canonical base
fact layer over the `pyDEXPI` full graph, and add a hand-authored generic graph
utility layer plus repo-owned edge-family classification policy in Souffle.

This slice should prove the substrate over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture
corpus, document the contract sharply, and establish the behavioral test seams
that later pump-specific rules, rule packs, and AI-assisted rule synthesis can
rely on.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want DEXPI 1.3 to be the explicit authoritative input contract, so that the repository does not imply support for a different semantic ingestion model than the code actually uses.
2. As a maintainer, I want `pyDEXPI` to be treated as the trusted DEXPI 1.3 XML-to-graph extraction dependency, so that the project boundary between extraction and interpretation stays explicit.
3. As a rules author, I want the canonical base fact layer to mirror the `pyDEXPI` full graph, so that every downstream rule begins from a reproducible graph substrate.
4. As a rules author, I want the base export to remain intentionally verbose and generic, so that I do not lose evidence through premature schema curation.
5. As a maintainer, I want one persisted fact per extracted node, one per extracted edge, and one per attached attribute, so that the fact grain remains stable and auditable.
6. As a maintainer, I want previously unseen upstream attributes to survive export automatically, so that new DEXPI 1.3 fixture shapes do not break the substrate.
7. As a rules author, I want the base export to avoid convenience predicates such as `pump/1`, so that interpretation stays out of the persisted contract.
8. As a maintainer, I want the contract to be defined over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus, so that the substrate proves itself against real fixture breadth rather than one narrow example.
9. As a reviewer, I want the checked-in golden fixtures to be clearly documented as a seed set rather than the full contract boundary, so that future work does not mistake current goldens for full coverage.
10. As a rules author, I want the first derived Souffle layer to be generic and reusable, so that later rule families can build on it without rewriting graph logic.
11. As a rules author, I want reusable edge-family predicates such as `composition_edge/3` and `reference_edge/3`, so that downstream rules do not repeatedly join raw edge attributes by hand.
12. As a rules author, I want a cautious `candidate_topology_edge/3` predicate, so that topology traversal can begin before the project commits to a stronger process-topology interpretation.
13. As a rules author, I want family-specific direct adjacency helpers, so that each rule can choose the correct traversal semantics explicitly.
14. As a rules author, I want a simple recursive `reachable/2` predicate over candidate topology edges, so that I can ask whether something is downstream without building full path provenance first.
15. As a maintainer, I want the first utility layer to stay small and explicit, so that it does not accumulate broad helper predicates before real rules require them.
16. As a maintainer, I want the edge-family classification policy to live in Souffle, so that interpretation can evolve without changing the persisted export format.
17. As a reviewer, I want the derived graph semantics contract to name the initial predicate surface explicitly, so that the next implementation slice cannot drift into vague “some utilities later” language.
18. As a process engineer, I want verification to be documented as downstream of graph export plus derived semantics, so that the architecture is understood as layered rather than verifier-first.
19. As a maintainer, I want the contract docs to state clearly that convenience predicates and domain predicates belong in derived Souffle layers, so that no one silently moves interpretation into the exporter.
20. As a maintainer, I want outdated `DEXPI 2.0 semantic IR` language removed from the active glossary and contract docs, so that the written architecture matches the implemented boundary.
21. As a rules author, I want the first validation seam to be stable graph export over the DEXPI 1.3 corpus, so that later logic failures can be isolated from extraction/export failures.
22. As a rules author, I want the second validation seam to be focused tests over representative fixtures such as `E03`, `E06`, and `C01`, so that recursive and classified predicates can be checked against real graph shapes.
23. As a maintainer, I want synthetic examples to remain available for later isolated rule verification, so that future rule generation can be tested behaviorally and not only on noisy corpus fixtures.
24. As a future operator, I want later trusted rules to execute deterministically over the fact layer instead of relying on ad hoc AI answers, so that verification remains reproducible and auditable.
25. As a future AI-assisted rules author, I want a stable graph-mirrored substrate and reusable graph utilities, so that generated rules have a deterministic target surface to compile against.
26. As a compliance engineer, I want rule packs to remain distinct from policy source documents, so that natural-language standards can later synthesize candidate rules without being confused for executable logic.
27. As a reviewer, I want AI-generated rules to be treated as candidates that require behavioral examples, so that trust comes from deterministic execution rather than raw Datalog readability.
28. As a maintainer, I want the next slice to defer policy-document-to-rule-pack synthesis, so that the foundational substrate work is not swallowed by a much larger AI problem.
29. As a maintainer, I want the repo PRD and Beads issue record to describe the same substrate plan, so that future contributors do not read contradictory planning artifacts.
30. As an engineer extending the verifier later, I want explicit derived graph semantics contracts in the docs, so that new rule families can reuse the same vocabulary and testing seams.

## Implementation Decisions

- The authoritative input contract for this slice is DEXPI 1.3 only.
- `pyDEXPI` is the trusted extraction dependency for XML-to-graph conversion; this repository owns graph-to-facts export and Souffle-derived interpretation above that export.
- The canonical persisted layer is a graph-mirrored base fact layer over the `pyDEXPI` full graph rather than a raw XML fact tree or an early domain-curated schema.
- The canonical base fact layer is intentionally verbose and generic. It should preserve extracted nodes, extracted edges, and attached attributes without introducing rule-specific predicates.
- Unknown or newly observed upstream attributes should survive export automatically through generic attribute facts rather than causing schema failures.
- The canonical base layer should persist only the `pyDEXPI` full graph for now. Explicit raw XML containment facts are deferred unless a concrete future rule proves they are needed.
- The intended regression surface for the substrate is the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus, not only the current `E03`, `E06`, and `C01` golden seed set.
- The first derived Souffle layer should be hand-authored rather than generated from observed graph schema.
- The repo-owned classification policy should live in Souffle rather than in exporter code, so classified semantics can evolve without re-exporting the canonical fact layer.
- The initial derived predicate surface should be explicit: `composition_edge/3`, `reference_edge/3`, `candidate_topology_edge/3`, `downstream_candidate/2`, `downstream_composition/2`, `downstream_reference/2`, and `reachable/2`.
- `candidate_topology_edge/3` should be intentionally conservative rather than claiming that topology traversal is already fully trusted in every case.
- Direct adjacency helpers should stay family-specific. Broader union predicates such as `downstream/2` should be introduced only when a real rule or operator-facing query needs them.
- The first recursive utility should be `reachable/2` over `candidate_topology_edge/3`; ordered path reconstruction and full path provenance are deferred.
- Pump discharge YAML rules should sit above the generic base fact layer and derived graph semantics layer rather than embedding graph semantics themselves.
- Verification commands should be documented and treated as consumers of the export-plus-derived-semantics substrate, not as the primary architectural center.
- The rule trust model for later AI-assisted work should be behavioral: candidate rules become trustworthy only after deterministic execution against positive and negative examples.
- Single rules and rule packs remain distinct units. Individual rules are the unit of behavioral debugging; rule packs are the unit of versioned promotion and deployment.
- Policy source documents, rule packs, and rule-pack synthesis are distinct concepts and should remain separate in the glossary and contract docs.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should assert external behavior and stable contracts, not implementation details or private helper structure.
- The highest seam for this slice is the `export-facts` behavior over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus. Tests at this seam should verify deterministic persisted graph-mirrored facts, provenance, and automatic preservation of observed attributes.
- A second high seam should cover the derived graph semantics layer on representative fixtures such as `E03`, `E06`, and `C01`, validating classified edge families, family-specific downstream helpers, and recursive `reachable/2`.
- Later synthetic examples should be used for isolated rule-shape verification, but the current substrate slice should prefer real DEXPI 1.3 fixtures wherever possible.
- Tests should confirm that the base export does not emit convenience predicates or domain predicates in the persisted artifact contract.
- Tests should verify that the current checked-in golden fixtures remain a seed set and that broader corpus coverage can be expanded without redefining the base contract.
- Tests should confirm that the derived classification policy lives above the persisted export and can change without changing the base fact artifact shape.
- Documentation-facing tests or fixture assertions should continue to use the repo’s existing black-box style around CLI commands and persisted artifacts rather than internal function mocks.
- Prior art already exists in the repository for export-facts CLI tests, checked-in golden graph facts, compile-rule CLI tests, and verifier-suite artifact tests. The new tests should extend those existing seams instead of inventing lower-level unit seams.
- Future AI-assisted rule verification should rely on positive and negative examples evaluated by the deterministic engine, not human review of raw Datalog syntax.

## Out of Scope

- DEXPI 2.0 as an active ingestion contract.
- A raw XML fact layer or XML-tree-first substrate.
- Automatic generation of domain predicates from unseen graph shapes.
- Full path reconstruction or ordered path evidence in the first derived utility slice.
- Pump-specific or rule-specific domain predicates in the persisted base export.
- DEXPI 1.2 as part of the current canonical substrate contract.
- Policy-document-to-rule-pack synthesis.
- Operator-facing dropdown UX for rule or rule-pack selection.
- Trusting AI to answer operator verification questions directly without deterministic execution.
- Human approval workflows for AI-generated rules beyond the defined behavioral-verification model.

## Further Notes

- The most important architectural protection in this slice is the boundary between generic persisted facts and derived Souffle interpretation.
- The base fact layer should be allowed to be verbose if that preserves reproducibility and future extensibility.
- The current checked-in documentation cleanup is part of the work because stale contract language would otherwise undermine the implementation slice.
- This PRD intentionally narrows the next step to substrate work. Richer operator rules, compliance rule packs, and AI-assisted synthesis remain downstream consumers of this layer rather than part of it.
close_reason: Completed DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate, corpus coverage, derived graph semantics, verifier integration, behavioral harness, and documentation reframing; validation passed with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests.
